step.analyze.blobs.name: Blob analysis
step.analyze.blobs.desc: Find objects in a binary mask and filter by area in the current image. Report centers in original-image coordinates.
step.analyze.contours.name: Contour analysis
step.analyze.contours.desc: Trace the outside of white regions, optionally as simpler polygons. Useful for comparing shapes.
step.analyze.histogram_stats.name: Region brightness statistics
step.analyze.histogram_stats.desc: Measure mean brightness and standard deviation in a selected region without changing the image. Useful for comparing lighting.
step.color.brightness_contrast.name: Brightness and contrast
step.color.brightness_contrast.desc: Adjust overall brightness and the difference between light and dark. Useful for dim or low-contrast images.
step.color.channel.name: View one channel
step.color.channel.desc: View one color channel to explore what BGR, HSV and LAB each describe.
step.color.clahe.name: Local contrast (CLAHE)
step.color.clahe.desc: Improve contrast in small regions while limiting noise amplification. Useful for uneven lighting.
step.color.gamma.name: Gamma correction
step.color.gamma.desc: Adjust midtones: gamma above 1 brightens them. Useful for seeing dark details while preserving black and white.
step.color.grayscale.name: Grayscale
step.color.grayscale.desc: Convert colors to brightness so you can focus on shapes and light.
step.color.hsv_mask.name: HSV color mask
step.color.hsv_mask.desc: Find colors by hue, saturation and brightness. For red across H=0, set the lower H above the upper H.
step.color.invert.name: Invert
step.color.invert.desc: Reverse the brightness of every channel. Useful for swapping the foreground and background of a mask.
step.color.lab_mask.name: LAB color mask
step.color.lab_mask.desc: Find objects using lightness L and color channels A/B. These controls use OpenCV values from 0 to 255.
step.edge.canny.name: Canny edges
step.edge.canny.desc: Find connected brightness boundaries, optionally on the image. Useful for studying object outlines.
step.edge.sobel.name: Sobel gradient
step.edge.sobel.desc: Measure brightness changes along x or y, or combine both to reveal edges.
step.edge_sim.jpeg.name: Simulate JPEG compression
step.edge_sim.jpeg.desc: Compress and decode the image to explore detail loss and block artifacts from low-quality JPEG.
step.edge_sim.noise.name: Simulate sensor noise
step.edge_sim.noise.desc: Add random Gaussian noise, with strength as its standard deviation. Useful for testing tolerance to noisy pixels.
step.edge_sim.resolution.name: Simulate low resolution
step.edge_sim.resolution.desc: Reduce pixel count, optionally enlarging for display, to explore detail loss in small cameras.
step.edge_sim.rgb565.name: Simulate RGB565
step.edge_sim.rgb565.desc: Use 5 bits for red and blue and 6 for green to explore color banding from fewer colors.
step.edge_sim.sensor.name: Edge camera simulation
step.edge_sim.sensor.desc: Combine resolution, RGB565, JPEG, noise and blur to explore image degradation. Device profiles are teaching examples, not calibrated hardware models.
step.filter.bilateral.name: Bilateral filter
step.filter.bilateral.desc: Smooth similar colors while preserving boundaries. Useful when reducing noise without losing outlines.
step.filter.gaussian_blur.name: Gaussian blur
step.filter.gaussian_blur.desc: Smooth noise using nearby pixels. Useful before thresholding or edge detection.
step.filter.median_blur.name: Median blur
step.filter.median_blur.desc: Replace a pixel with the middle value of its neighbors. Useful for removing isolated black and white specks.
step.filter.sharpen.name: Sharpen
step.filter.sharpen.desc: Emphasize details and edges in slightly blurred images. High amounts also amplify noise.
step.geometry.crop.name: Percentage crop
step.geometry.crop.desc: Keep a region selected as percentages of the image. Use this to remove distracting borders.
step.geometry.flip.name: Flip
step.geometry.flip.desc: Mirror the image horizontally or vertically. Use this to correct a mirrored or upside-down view.
step.geometry.resize.name: Resize
step.geometry.resize.desc: Resize by a scale factor or exact dimensions. Smaller images can make later steps faster.
step.geometry.roi.name: Region of interest
step.geometry.roi.desc: Mark the area you want to observe, or keep only that area. Useful for studying one part of a scene.
step.geometry.rotate.name: Rotate
step.geometry.rotate.desc: Turn the image counterclockwise by a preset or custom angle. Use this to correct camera orientation.
step.geometry.rotate.expand: Expand canvas to keep full image
step.morph.close.name: Close
step.morph.close.desc: Grow then shrink white regions to fill small holes in objects.
step.morph.dilate.name: Dilate
step.morph.dilate.desc: Grow white regions to fill small gaps or connect broken lines.
step.morph.erode.name: Erode
step.morph.erode.desc: Shrink white regions to remove tiny specks or separate touching objects.
step.morph.gradient.name: Morphological gradient
step.morph.gradient.desc: Compare grown and shrunken regions to reveal object boundaries.
step.morph.open.name: Open
step.morph.open.desc: Shrink then grow white regions to remove specks while preserving larger objects.
step.motion.background_sub.name: Background subtraction
step.motion.background_sub.desc: Learn the background over time and highlight changes. Useful for detecting moving objects with a stationary camera.
step.motion.frame_diff.name: Frame difference
step.motion.frame_diff.desc: Compare grayscale brightness with the previous frame and report a mean difference from 0 to 255. The first frame sets the baseline.
step.motion.still_detect.name: Stillness detection
step.motion.still_detect.desc: Report stillness after N consecutive mean frame differences fall below the threshold. The baseline frame does not count; use this for automatic capture.
step.threshold.adaptive.name: Adaptive threshold
step.threshold.adaptive.desc: Choose a threshold for each neighborhood. Useful for text or shapes under uneven lighting.
step.threshold.binary.name: Fixed threshold
step.threshold.binary.desc: Split an image into black and white using a brightness threshold. Useful when objects and background differ in brightness.
step.threshold.otsu.name: Otsu threshold
step.threshold.otsu.desc: Choose a threshold automatically. Useful when image brightness forms two groups.
